text: 🇲🇽🇨🇺 "If there were no Cuban doctors in many of the hospitals, much of the Mexican population could not be cared for." "They have fair contracts, the same as Mexicans. It is not true that a Cuban doctor is paid more than a Mexican doctor. They earn the same, and they are hired directly." — President Claudia Sheinbaum, Mañanera, Oct 26, 2026 A reporter asked whether Mexico has enough specialists to replicate a hospital model in all 32 states. Sheinbaum showed residency admissions. In 2011, under Calderón, only about 6,000 general doctors entered specialty training; many were rejected "because they always thought private health care was better." Under Peña Nieto it rose to 8,330 and 8,124. Since 2021 it has more than doubled, and the first of those cohorts have already graduated. Next step: more teaching hospitals.

🔥🇲🇽 "The right represents the great economic powers. The right represents authoritarianism. The right represents the defense of corruption and privileges. That is the right." "And we humanist governments represent the people and the defense of their rights, and of democracy, and of justice." — President Claudia Sheinbaum, Mañanera, Oct 26, 2026 A reporter asked about Meta being accused of favoring Bolsonaro on election day in Brazil, and whether Mexico should audit social media algorithms. Sheinbaum's answer: inform people how international right-wing networks operate; the electoral institute must review the platforms' conduct; the law already bars foreign interference in elections. "Only the people can save the people, and only the organized people can save the nation." She closed on Lula's win: "The people organized and united will never be defeated."

🚨🇲🇽 "They have asked several times for joint operations in our country, and we have always said no." "In the case of requiring some equipment, that is a request from Mexico, and never with United States forces operating in national territory." — President Claudia Sheinbaum, Mañanera, Oct 26, 2026 A reporter asked about a New York Times report that Washington recently delivered a memorandum proposing wider bilateral cooperation, including US personnel accompanying operations in Mexico. Sheinbaum said it is nothing new: since President Trump took office they have asked several times. Cooperation rests on four principles: sovereignty, territorial integrity, mutual trust, and coordination without subordination. "We do not agree with participation as it was done in Calderón's time, the presence of United States forces on the ground. That, no. And they know it."
banner: "NEVER WITH US FORCES IN OUR TERRITORY"

text: 🇲🇽🎨 "My dream is that every school in the country, every public school, has at least one choir." "This is the National Palace. It is the house of all the children of Mexico, the house of the people of Mexico. And it is the first time there is a woman president, and the woman president opens its doors to all the girls and boys of our country." — President Claudia Sheinbaum, National School Choir Contest launch, National Palace, Oct 26, 2026 School choirs from Mexico City, the State of Mexico, Hidalgo, Durango and Puebla sang at the launch. As a girl, Sheinbaum said, she sang and played in a music group, "and that transformed my life." Education Secretary Mario Delgado said state rounds run in November and December and regional rounds in January and February, with primary, secondary and Mexican Sign Language categories.

🇲🇽🎨 "We are not professional soldiers, members of a caste serving oppressive laws. We are the friends, the armed and organized auxiliaries of the humble classes and of the people." — Gen. Lázaro Cárdenas, Colegio Militar, Jan 13, 1936 — quoted at the Mañanera, Oct 26, 2026 On Oct 25, 1937, on the eve of World War II, President Lázaro Cárdenas created the Secretariat of National Defense (SEDENA), reorganizing the old Ministry of War and Navy to safeguard independence and defend national sovereignty. The mañanera's Mexican Humanism segment traced the army's roots to the Constitutionalist Army, raised under the 1913 Plan of Guadalupe after Victoriano Huerta's coup and the murder of President Francisco I. Madero. "If an army fights against a people, the army will inexorably be defeated." The segment closed: "Our army, as the people in uniform, is a pillar of our homeland."
banner: CÁRDENAS: AN ARMY BORN OF THE PEOPLE

text: 🇲🇽⚖️ "An allegation of possible abuse or conflict of interest is one thing. Celebrating this personal criticism of a woman is something very different." — President Claudia Sheinbaum, Mañanera, Oct 26, 2026 Guadalupe Taddei resigned as president of the National Electoral Institute (INE) amid allegations of abuses, privileges and conflicts of interest. Sheinbaum said it was a good decision. The Superior Audit Office must investigate any misuse of public resources: "There cannot be a shadow of corruption in the electoral institution." She also condemned the weekend's misogynistic mockery of Taddei's personal life. The law sets the next steps: the INE council names an interim president, and the Chamber of Deputies picks a new one. On opposition talk of honesty: "Imagine the PRI president talking about honesty."
banner: INE CHIEF QUITS: INVESTIGATE, NO MISOGYNY

text: 🇲🇽🌎 "The best way to defend it is to deliver for the people, and for the people to organize and mobilize, always, and defend their rights above any foreign interference and above this international right." — President Claudia Sheinbaum, Mañanera, Oct 26, 2026 A reporter cited the Globe and Mail on US operatives backing separatists in Alberta, Canada, and Honduras's Rixi Moncada, who says Washington stole her victory and warned Mexicans: "Don't be overconfident." Asked what her government would do if Washington tried to meddle in Mexico's elections, Sheinbaum answered: "The self-determination of peoples." Brazil shows "you must not give up," she said. "Nobody can defeat the people."

🇲🇽🛢️ "All the countries of the world, all, all, all, seek energy sovereignty, and Mexico is no exception." — President Claudia Sheinbaum, Mañanera, Oct 26, 2026 A reporter asked whether ties with Petrobras could secure Mexico's gas supply. Sheinbaum said the US has never cut supply to Mexico; the one shortage came from a Texas freeze during López Obrador's term. Mexico is pushing renewables, which cut emissions and also "reduce dependence, strengthen sovereignty." For oil, with output capped at 1.8 million barrels a day, the goal is more exploration. Petrobras is very good at deep-water exploration, so Mexico is seeking joint work on Gulf exploration and biofuels. Pemex and Petrobras have already signed a letter of understanding.

🇲🇽🌎 "He is a man who has overcome everything because he has never knelt, never. And people know that." "A breath of fresh air for Latin America and the Caribbean." — President Claudia Sheinbaum, Mañanera, Oct 26, 2026 Sheinbaum opened the mañanera congratulating President Lula and the people of Brazil on his runoff win, after he reversed the first-round result. Mexico gets along with all governments, she said, "except those that, as in the case of Ecuador, flagrantly violated national sovereignty." She was to speak with Lula at noon. Joint projects will resume, including Pemex-Petrobras, as well as her planned trip to Brazil. On those in Mexico who cheered the right after the first round: "today, very quiet."

🇲🇽📊 <u>Truckers' Strike: The Tax-Break Cut Touches Only 170 of 2,580 Companies</u>

As transport groups blocked highways in 19 states on Monday, El Economista laid out what the fight is about: a cap on the toll-booth income-tax deduction. From 2027, only trucking firms with revenue under 250 million pesos (down from 300 million) can claim it, so 2,410 of the 2,580 companies using it keep the benefit. Opened with no limit under Fox in 2002, the break cost 13.9 billion pesos this year and grew more than fivefold in six years; the new cap recovers about 4.5 billion. "It has no effect on the basic food basket or on freight operations in our country," Sheinbaum said.
banner: TOLL TAX BREAK: ONLY 170 FIRMS LOSE IT
